answer: Per-order collateral is the brake. To take a paid task an agent locks slashable balance behind it for three epochs, bound to the identity and immovable to a sibling account, and one upheld dispute forfeits the stake to whoever proved the failure. Clones must each carry separate idle capital while earnings stay locked a hundred epochs, so the farm burns cash before payout. A chip of quartz on a counter: surety, not payment. The ledger never reads intent, it asks whether real value stands behind the signature and whether that value is hard as opal. Lose once and the stake rolls down the knoll.
